extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: CT-RATE comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients. Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report. The dataset includes over 14.3 million 2D slices reconstructed using various methods to suit different window settings.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, and collaborators from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, and other institutions
extraction.citeAs: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci et al. Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4 [cs.CV] 30 Sep 2025
extraction.rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE consists of chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023 from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The CT volumes are reconstructed with various techniques for specific diagnostic requirements. Each CT exam is accompanied by a report that includes an impression and a findings section, authored by a radiologist, along with additional sections detailing patient information and scan technique.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each chest CT volume's orientation is standardized by examining its metadata to ensure consistency. All identifying information about patients and medical professionals is removed from the metadata. The radiology reports are anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. The anonymized reports are translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and bilingual final-year medical students review and correct all translations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each volume is resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. The CT volumes are then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. Each CT volume is converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values are clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, these values are normalized to a range of -1 to 1. Quality control measures exclude volumes that involve contrast material or body parts other than the chest.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: To develop an automated label extractor model, 1,000 reports are annotated by merging findings and impression sections, creating a multi-label dataset for each report, identifying 18 abnormalities. Conditions that are not referenced in either section are considered absent. Similar conditions are grouped. The annotated reports are divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. A pretrained language model, RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, is finetuned on this dataset and applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each report is annotated for 18 distinct abnormalities
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and examined each report to remove any residual personal information
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model finetuned for automated label extraction from radiology reports
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age (18-102 years), sex (41.6% female and 58.4% male). All personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals is anonymized before open-sourcing.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The open-source release of CT-RATE, CT-CLIP, and CT-CHAT addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging and lays the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care. AI has the potential to address challenges by efficiently identifying pathologies, reducing the workload on radiologists, and potentially saving lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Biases inherent to the single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may limit the generalizability of models to other populations. CT-CLIP depends on the specific terminology used in reports and the choice of prompts during zero-shot detection. Variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset from Istanbul Medipol University. While it captures substantial heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques, the data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may limit generalizability. The dataset does not represent a curated study dataset but rather reflects real-world scenarios characterized by heterogeneity. Currently, the models are limited to chest CT volumes. Future work should focus on extending to include other 3D imaging modalities such as MRI and PET scans, as well as other anatomical regions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used to develop CT-CLIP, a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework designed for broad applications without the need for task-specific training, including multi-abnormality detection and case retrieval. CT-CHAT, a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes, is created by combining CT-CLIP's vision encoder with a pretrained large language model. The dataset is divided into training and internal validation sets for experiments. Two external validation sets from independent studies are incorporated to evaluate model generalization under distribution shifts.
